title: Your First Struct
story: You found a lost digital profile card. It has a name slot and an age slot — but the card is blank. You need to fill it in so the profile system can display it!
why: Structs let you bundle related data into a single named type, keeping information organized and easy to pass around.
analogy: A struct is like a form you fill out — it has labeled fields for each piece of information. Once filled, the whole form travels together as one unit.
try_it: Create a Person struct for your best friend. Add a third field called `hobby: Str`. Print all three fields.
tips: Use semicolons between fields in the type definition, commas when creating an instance
Field access uses dot notation: `my_person.name` — no brackets or parentheses
Type names use PascalCase (Person), field names use snake_case (first_name)
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons between fields in the type definition — `{ name: Str; age: Int; }` not `{ name: Str, age: Int }`
Using parentheses instead of braces for creation: `Person( ... )` is wrong, use `Person{ ... }`
Trying to print the whole struct with `io.println(my_friend)` — print individual fields instead
